args.text:
MISSION COMPLETE — BESS fault identified, restored within my authority, verified, rover home and stowed.

1) INSPECTION (what was observed)
- Unit telemetry (power_status, twice: before and after intervention) across all five serviced units: PDU-1 (habitat life support, crew-critical), PDU-2 (comms, mission-critical), PDU-3 (science, non-critical) and the ISRU plant were all breaker=closed, energized=true, trip_cause=null, resets=0.
- BESS (base energy storage, mission-critical) was the failed unit: breaker=tripped, energized=false, trip_cause=OVERCURRENT, resets_since_start=0, module BAT-0101 in bess_cradle/tray.
- On site at the BESS view pose (33.38, 14.3, yaw 0) the front camera confirmed the service-panel status lamp RED, with no scorching, burn marks or open covers on the unit or battery racks.
- Manifest: BAT-0101 recorded serviceable in the cradle; spare BAT-0102 available at depot_spares_stand/slot_0.

2) DECISION AND ACTION (what was done)
- Chose the least-invasive restoration first: a single breaker reset, which is mine to do. - press on bess_panel/press: verified effect `pressed` HOLDS — tool on the fitted button axis (off-axis 0.0002 m), jaws closed, 0.0063 m past the button face, then retreated 0.697 m.

- One anomaly is on the log and is explained, not open: the final dock_to_pose call returned "no progress for 20.0s; dist 0.006 m, yaw_err 0.030 rad" — i.e. the servo reported failure because the base was already inside tolerance and had nothing left to close. - Root cause of the OVERCURRENT trip was not diagnosed beyond the trip record: the reset cleared it and BESS has held energized, but the cause (transient load event vs. early BAT-0101 degradation) is unknown from the evidence available to me. Recommend ground review of BESS current telemetry; if it trips again, the next step is a BAT-0101 → BAT-0102 swap, which will require authorization while the unit is energized.
